model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, representing ACC (%), spans from 40 to 65 in linear increments. The 'Base' method is shown as a black solid line with circle markers, starting at approximately 39% and rising to about 44%, remaining relatively flat thereafter. The 'MEND' method, depicted as a brown dashed line with diamond markers, begins near 45% and rises to approximately 57%. The 'FT' method, shown as a blue dashed line with triangle markers, starts at about 40% and increases to around 48%. The 'MEMIT' method, represented by a purple dashed line with circle markers, begins near 45% and climbs to about 55%. The 'IKE' method, shown as a red dashed line with triangle markers, starts at approximately 43% and increases to about 50%. The 'ROME' method, displayed as a green dashed line with square markers, begins at around 51% and rises steadily to approximately 66%.
